newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - August 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
GOVERNMENT SAYS THERE WAS NO DECISION TO PUT OFF PAY HIKE

The government was criticised in parliament Tuesday for reportedly deciding to withhold the implementation of revised pay scales for its employees. But Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said there was no change in the government's policy on implementing the revised pay scales and that a decision would be taken soon. He said no particular date was fixed for issuing the notification although in accordance with the decision already taken it would be effective from August 1. Chidambaram said the prime minister had only suggested to the cabinet secretary to withhold notification since the subject was to be discussed by parliament on Tuesday.
Indian Express
BATTLE HOTS UP IN BHARATIYA JANATA PARTY

The Bharatiya Janata Party leadership's efforts to present a united face is being threatened in Delhi where former Chief Minister Madan Lal Khurana and Chief Minister Sahib Singh Verma are locked in a battle for power. Party President L.K. Advani and senior party leader Atal Behari Vajpayee together castigated the two rivals in a meeting on Saturday. But their efforts for a third alternative to the chief ministership is proving difficult to implement. For Khurana his battle would be half won if Verma were removed and someone else installed as chief minister. The party leadership, with the support of the Rashtriya Swyamsevak Sangh organisation, had refused to reinstate Khurana since a case is pending against him in the Supreme Court.
The Economic Times
EXPORT GROWTH TARGET SET AT 10 PCT TO 15 PCT

India has revised its export growth target of 20 percent for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) to 10 to 15 percent due to a fall in export growth in the first quarter of the year, Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said. He said the government would try to boost exports in the remaining three quarters to achieve a growth target of at least 15 percent. Exports in the first quarter of fiscal 1997/98 fell by 0.95 percent. The export target fixed for 1997/98 was $39 billion. The new target is about $36 billion.
PLAN TO MAKE GOLD A FREELY TRADABLE FINANCIAL ASSET

The government is working on a policy framework to make gold a freely tradable financial asset. Banks will be allowed to act as intermediaries and will buy gold paying dollars. This will indirectly reduce the pressure on the Reserve Bank of India which is the only agency responsible for absorbing excess dollars to manage exchange rate stability. The banks will be allowed to import gold from the international market and pay for it in dollars. An official said this would indirectly result in excess dollars getting sucked out through the purchase of gold, which is both liquid and a good hedge against inflation.
Financial Express
DIVIDEND WARRANTS OF MANY FIRMS CANCELLED

The State Bank of India (SBI) began cancelling majority of interest or dividend warrant accounts of corporates including AAA-rated non-banking finance companies (NBFCs) and manufacturing firms with it. The SBI holds about 50 percent of the dividend or interest warrant servicing business. Many companies collecting fixed deposits from the public have depended on the wide branch network of the SBI for servicing the monthly interest payment on deposits through the at-par facility offered by the bank. With the SBI cancelling such facilities, hundreds of thousands of fixed deposit investors in these companies now hold worthless interest warrants.
NATIONAL BOURSE SUSPENDS PRE-OPENING AND CLOSING SESSIONS

The National bourse suspended the pre-opening and the newly introduced closing sessions at the bourse. But it will extend trading hours on Tuesday by half an hour for the normal trading session. This will not be a closing session. It will now have trading hours from 9:30 a.m. to 3 p.m. except on Tuesdays. On Tuesdays the trading will close at 3:30 p.m. in the afternoon. The decision was taken because of the lack of interest on the part of the members and due to a communication satellite dislocation which has limited the time that is available to the exchange for operating its trading system.
MINISTRIES AGREE ON RISK SHARING FOR LIQUID FUEL SUPPLIES

The ministries of power and petroleum agreed on commitment charges and liquidated damages in the fuel supply agreement for the liquid fuel based power plants. The two agreed on an eight percent premium on the cost of fuel supplied to independent power producers (IPPs). The ministries also concurred that the national oil companies should pay liquidated damages equal to the fixed cost of the power generated by the IPPs. In case of any slippage in fuel supply, the oil companies should pay five percent rebate on the cost of fuel to the IPPs.
Business Standard
BOMBAY BOURSE INDICATOR GAINS 82.65 POINTS

The Bombay bourse's sensitive index gained 82.65 points Tuesday over the previous close to register a 34-month high of 4,548.02 points. The market sentiments were perked up by fresh buying by foreign institutional investors. India's Global Depository Receipts markets showed a distinct upswing in recent trading sessions and marketmen say this helped the bull run to continue in local markets. Trading sentiment at the National bourse firmed up further on account of hectic buying by foreign institutional investors, coupled with front running punters. The National bourse index shot up by 22.75 points to close at 1,273.15 points.
CABINET CLEARS DRAFT COMPANIES BILL

The cabinet cleared the draft companies bill, paving the way for its introduction in the current session of parliament. It provides for buyback of shares by companies with adequate safeguards, simplification of depreciation rates, limits for secretarial compliance and provisions for the maintenance of cost data. The bill also proposes to tighten entry norms for companies seeking registration. Private companies which want to register should have minimum capital of 100,000 rupees and government companies which want to register should have minimum capital of 50 million rupees.
HINDUSTAN LEVER DEFENDS SHARE PURCHASE

Hindustan Lever chairman K.B. Dadiseth defended the company's purchase of 800,000 shares of Brooke Bond Lipton (BBLIL) a month before the merger of the two. He said the company would raise the issue at an appropriate forum. The shares where bought from the Unit Trust of India in March 1996. Dadiseth said the company had obtained legal opinion that a company buying shares of its associate company could not be interpreted as insider trading. The bourse regulator on Monday asked for an explanation from the company for the purchase of these shares.
The Observer
CUSTOMS MAY AUCTION DAEWOO'S CAR KITS

Following Daewoo's failure to pay customs duty and take possession of about 600 containers of completely knocked down kits for its Ceilo cars, it has to pay a customs duty of about 300 million rupees to take delivery of the containers. The Customs Department has threatened to auction the consignment if Daewoo fails to take delivery by the end of September. A senior customs official said these containers were lying with the Container Corporation for more than a year. Officials at the Container Corporation said the Daewoo Motor Corporation failed to take delivery of the containers despite repeated reminders.
